citations.B1: Read-then-write is not atomic — two threads can both read 99 and both return True, letting the limit be exceeded
citations.B3: wrap the read/increment in a `threading.Lock` (or use an atomic backend op)
citations.B4: There is no time window, so this is a lifetime quota, not a rate limit
citations.B5: The dict grows without bound, one entry per distinct `user_id` — a memory leak
citations.B6: State is per-process, so with N workers the real limit is N×`limit`
